software: CFOUR interfaced with the OpenMMPol library
basis_set: 6-31G(d) for geometry optimization, 6-31+G(d) for excited-state calculations
active_space_orbital_description: all orbitals selected by the unrestricted natural orbital occupation criterion plus additional pi orbitals of the conjugated chromophore
active_space_protocol: unrestricted natural orbitals (UNOs) used as the initial guess and as the automatic active-space selector: include all orbitals with natural occupation numbers between 0.01 and 1.99, reducing the set if the resulting space is too large. nroots_per_mult: 2 states state-averaged (3 for the Amber-embedding calculation)
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: S0. First excitation energy at SA-CAS(12,12)/6-31+G(d) on CASSCF geometries: vacuum 3.41; Amber 3.48; AMOEBA at the Amber geometry 3.63 (3.65 with the state-specific correction); AMOEBA at the AMOEBA geometry 3.50 (3.58 state-specific corrected) eV. TDCAM-B3LYP/6-31+G(d) on the same CASSCF geometries: 3.15, 3.13, 3.22, 3.24 eV; on DFT geometries: 3.04, 3.22, 3.30, 3.16 eV. compound_name: Free d- and f-block metal ions (3d, 4d and 5d transition metal ions in various oxidation states, and trivalent lanthanide ions), assessed as a minimal-active-space reference set
metal_center: 3d, 4d and 5d transition metals and trivalent f-block ions (Eu(III), Gd(III) and Tb(III) excluded for cost)
metal_ox_state: various, spanning the common oxidation states of each block; trivalent for the f-block ions
d_electron_count: all dn configurations for the transition metal ions and all fn configurations for the trivalent lanthanides
ligand_set: none (free ions)
point_group: spherical symmetry enforced with the ATOM supersymmetry keyword for the optimized atomic orbitals
geometry_source: free ions, no geometry
method: minimal active space CASSCF-SO: state-averaged CASSCF followed by state interaction with spin-orbit coupling; MS-CASPT2 and XMS-CASPT2 additionally performed for Co(II) and Pr(III) to show the effect of dynamic correlation; results recast into Slater-Condon and spin-orbit coupling parameters in the Russell-Saunders basis and compared with experiment, AILFT and ligand-field DFT
relativistic_treatment: scalar relativistic Hamiltonian (two-component decoupling of the four-component Dirac Hamiltonian) with atomic mean-field integrals (AMFI) for the spin-orbit Hamiltonian
soc_included: yes, spin-orbit coupling introduced by state interaction after variational spin-free orbital optimization
active_space_orbital_description: the minimal active space: n electrons in the five d orbitals for the d-block, or n electrons in the seven f orbitals for the f-block, where n is the dn or fn configuration of the ion
active_space_protocol: minimal active space, (n,5) for d-block ions and (n,7) for f-block ions, state-averaged over all possible roots for every spin multiplicity of the given configuration; (X)MS-CASPT2 on all SA-CASSCF roots with an imaginary shift of 0.1 for the Co(II) and Pr(III) comparisons
multiplicities_studied: all possible spin multiplicities of each dn or fn configuration
nroots_per_mult: all roots of each configuration and multiplicity
Other: This is the reference assessment of when the ubiquitous minimal active space is good enough. Spin-orbit coupling constants: reproduced to within about 200 cm-1 of experimentally derived values, which is usually under 10 percent error for 4dn, 5dn and 4fn configurations but up to 30 percent for 3dn; the abstract-level summary is overestimation by 5-30 percent for 3d ions, within plus or minus 10 percent for 4d and 5d ions, and overestimation by 2-10 percent for trivalent 4f ions. Slater-Condon parameters are typically overestimated by 20-50 percent (with some 3d outliers underestimated by 1-20 percent) because of the missing dynamic correlation, so the authors explicitly do not recommend minimal active space CASSCF-SO where accurate term excitation energies are needed, and recommend CASPT2 or NEVPT2 instead for quantitative work. The Slater-Condon error is systematic for divalent 4d and trivalent 4f ions, so simple scaling may be viable there when resources are limited, but this does not hold for 3d ions. The spin-orbit coupling constant varies quadratically with atomic number Z at fixed dn configuration, and also for the trivalent lanthanides even though the configuration changes with Z
reference_short: Walisinghe and Chilton, Assessment of minimal active space CASSCF-SO methods for calculation of atomic Slater-Condon and spin-orbit coupling parameters in d- and f-block ions, Dalton Trans. 50, 14130 (2021)
notes: Mined from OA text by claude-casscf-data_mining. Free ions rather than coordination compounds, and covering many ions at once, so this is entered as a single reference row rather than one row per ion; active_space_nel is left empty because it varies with the ion. Directly relevant to active-space selection: it quantifies the accuracy ceiling of the (n,5)/(n,7) minimal space that underpins most single_aniso and AILFT work on real complexes.

compound_name: V(acac)3, tris(acetylacetonato)vanadium(III)
ligand_set: three bidentate acetylacetonate (acac) chelates, pseudo-octahedral O6
geometry_source: optimized with Kohn-Sham DFT using the revM06-L functional and def2-TZVP basis, with frequency analysis confirming a local minimum; gas phase
method: two-stage spin-orbit-inclusive multiconfiguration pair-density functional theory: stage one is spin-orbit-free CASCI or CMS-PDFT on two spin manifolds using orbitals from CASSCF, SA-CASSCF or WSA-CASSCF; stage two adds spin-orbit coupling by state interaction (RASSI) over all degenerate components of the retained roots
software: OpenMolcas 21.02 for the multiconfigurational calculations; locally modified Gaussian 16 Revision C.01 for the DFT geometries
basis_set: ANO-RCC-VTZP for the transition metal, oxygen and nitrogen; ANO-RCC-VDZP for carbon; ANO-RCC-MB for hydrogen and fluorine; auxiliary basis sets for the two-electron integrals; def2-TZVP for the DFT geometries
relativistic_treatment: second-order Douglas-Kroll-Hess (DKH2) for the scalar relativistic terms
soc_included: yes, added by state interaction over the two spin manifolds after spin-orbit-free orbital optimization
active_space_orbital_description: the valence d electrons in the five metal d orbitals
active_space_protocol: (2,5) valence-d minimal space used identically for CASSCF, SA-CASSCF and WSA-CASSCF; the three orbital-optimization schemes differ only in the state weighting, with WSA-CASSCF putting 90 percent weight on the lowest state of each spin manifold and spreading 10 percent over the rest. For V(acac)3 all five d orbitals are retained even by state-specific CASSCF.
nroots_per_mult: 15 singlet and 10 triplet roots carried into the spin-orbit state interaction
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: triplet. Zero-field splitting D (cm-1), SA-CASSCF/CASCI -13.64, SA-CASSCF/CMS-PDFT 13.85, CASSCF/CASCI 4.90, CASSCF/CMS-PDFT 4.96, WSA-CASSCF/CASCI 6.82, WSA-CASSCF/CMS-PDFT 7.75, experiment 7.47
Other: Spin-orbit lowering of the ground state: -35 cm-1 with SA-CASSCF orbitals, -15 with CASSCF, -19 with WSA-CASSCF; SA-CASSCF badly overestimates the SOC contribution here and even gets the sign of D wrong. One of the three molecules used for the ground-state-weight sensitivity scan, which shows a discontinuous jump in D near 25 percent weight. Core finding of the study, which is about how the orbitals are optimized rather than about the active space size: state-specific CASSCF orbitals beat conventional equal-weight SA-CASSCF orbitals, but state-specific optimization can rotate d orbitals that are empty in the ground state out of the active space entirely (this happens for Cr(acac)3 and Mo(acac)3, where two unoccupied d orbitals are lost even from a good initial guess, although the SCF itself converges). The proposed weighted-state-averaged CASSCF fixes this by putting 90 percent of the weight on the lowest state of each spin manifold and spreading the remaining 10 percent evenly over the others; all five d orbitals are then retained. Mean percentage absolute deviation in D across the set: SA-CASSCF/CASCI 102 percent, SA-CASSCF/CMS-PDFT 138, CASSCF/CASCI 39, CASSCF/CMS-PDFT 90, WSA-CASSCF/CASCI 27, and WSA-CASSCF/CMS-PDFT 14 percent (mean percentage deviation 3 percent), making WSA-CASSCF/CMS-PDFT the recommended combination. The ground-state weight can be anywhere from 50 to 95 percent without significantly changing D. Fe(acac)3 is excluded from the mean errors because its experimental D is near zero. Geometry and solvation tests on Mn(acac)3 show that DFT-optimized gas-phase structures give essentially the same D as experimental structures.
reference_short: Wu, Zhou, Bao, Gagliardi and Truhlar, Zero-Field Splitting Calculations by Multiconfiguration Pair-Density Functional Theory, J. Chem. Theory Comput. (2022)
notes: Mined from OA text by claude-casscf-data_mining. Oxidation state and d-electron count follow arithmetically from the ligand charges and the stated active-space electron count. One of the two cases where conventional SA-CASSCF gives qualitatively wrong D. Note the paper writes the ligand as hfa (1,1,1,5,5,5-hexafluoro-2,4-pentanedione) in the abstract but hfc in the tables; the table spelling is kept here for traceability.

The calculated d-orbital splitting for the real complex closely resembles that of an idealized [CoBr5]3- square pyramid (ordering dxy, then dyz and dxz, then dz2, then dx2-y2) except that the dxz/dyz degeneracy is lifted by the lower real symmetry. compound_name: trans-3,4-dimethyl-1,2-dioxetane (TDMD), thermal decomposition to two acetaldehyde fragments, one electronically excited
geometry_source: O-O and C-C transition states optimized in this work with SA-CASSCF and MS-CASPT2; the 27 static configurations used for the benchmarking are structures sampled along the dynamical reaction path. Surface-hopping trajectories all start from the O-O transition state geometry rather than the reactant
method: SA-CASSCF state-averaged over S0, S1, S2, S3, T1, T2, T3 and T4, and MS-CASPT2, for potential energies and spin-orbit coupling matrix elements; fewest-switches trajectory surface hopping with energy-based decoherence correction for the nonadiabatic dynamics (0.5 fs velocity-Verlet steps, initial velocities Boltzmann-sampled at 300 K and rescaled to 3.84 eV of kinetic energy at the O-O transition state)
software: OpenMolcas 21.06 for energies, NACVs, gradients and SOC matrix elements, interfaced with SHARC 2.1 for the surface-hopping dynamics
basis_set: 6-31G, 6-31G* and ANO-RCC-VDZP for SA-CASSCF; ANO-RCC-VDZP for MS-CASPT2. SA-CASSCF/6-31G was chosen for the dynamics
active_space_orbital_description: the four sigma and four sigma* orbitals of the four-membered dioxetane ring, plus the two oxygen lone-pair occupied orbitals perpendicular to the ring
active_space_protocol: (12,10) built from the bonds that break: all four ring sigma and sigma* orbitals plus the two out-of-plane oxygen lone pairs, so that sequential O-O and C-C scission is described throughout. State-averaged over eight states (four singlets S0-S3 and four triplets T1-T4), which is what the near-degenerate entropic trap region requires
nroots_per_mult: 4 singlets and 4 triplets
Other: Basis-set benchmark against MS-CASPT2/ANO-RCC-VDZP over 27 configurations. MAEs of the energy gaps in kcal/mol for E(S1)-E(S0), E(T1)-E(S0), E(S1)-E(T1), E(T2)-E(S1): SA-CASSCF/6-31G 1.05, 0.99, 0.52, 1.67; SA-CASSCF/6-31G* 1.48, 1.49, 0.77, 2.14; SA-CASSCF/ANO-RCC-VDZP 1.57, 1.43, 0.93, 2.11. MAEs of the admixture coefficient magnitudes alpha(0,1), alpha(1,1), alpha(1,2): 6-31G 0.061, 0.119, 0.034; 6-31G* 0.074, 0.117, 0.039; ANO-RCC-VDZP 0.068, 0.118, 0.061. So the smallest basis, 6-31G, is the most accurate against MS-CASPT2 on both counts and was used for the dynamics. The dominant ACM differs between methods: alpha(1,1) for MS-CASPT2/ANO-RCC-VDZP but alpha(0,1) for SA-CASSCF/6-31G, and SA-CASSCF underestimates them - the MS-CASPT2 leading ACM averages 1.75 times the SA-CASSCF leading ACM, and its alpha(1,1) averages 2.69 times the SA-CASSCF alpha(1,1). The SA-CASSCF/6-31G SOC matrix elements were therefore scaled by a factor of 2. Zero-point energy of the O-O transition state 3.35 eV (SA-CASSCF). Trajectory outcome (297 trajectories): S0 194, S1 50, S2 0, S3 0, T1 53, T2 4, singlet excited states 50, triplet excited states 57; S0 quantum yield 0.645, triplet quantum yield 0.189 against an experimental 0.20, singlet quantum yield 0.166 against 0.101 from an earlier SA8-CASSCF(8,6)/STO-3G+6-31G* study.

The authors argue this suffices for the lowest metal-centred ligand-field transitions: plain CASSCF already gives the correct multiplet ordering and the ordering does not change when DDCI3+Q dynamic correlation is added, with CASSCF-vs-DDCI3+Q differences no larger than 0.42 eV (3 4Tg of the Co complex)
nroots_per_mult: 4 states reported per complex
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: 1 1Ag. 1 1Ag 0.00; 1 1Tg 0.94; 2 1Tg 1.78; 3 1Tg 2.19 (DDCI3+Q reference). CASSCF: 0.00, 0.73, 1.41, 2.05. Performance is markedly worse than for the organic chromophores in the same study. The open-shell Co(II) and Ni(II) complexes required the spin-density approach for srDFT.

point_group: D2h when planar, D2 when twisted
geometry_source: planar structure taken from Thiel's benchmark set (the paper's ref. 111); all bond lengths and angles held fixed while only the H-C-C-H dihedral was varied
method: SA-CASSCF plus CASSCF-DFT variants (CAS-srDFT and MC-PDFT, SA and CI-DFT flavours, with and without complex functional translation), benchmarked against internally contracted MRCI+Q

active_space_orbital_description: the valence pi and pi* orbitals and their two electrons

geometry_source: constructed models: all ethylene units at their ground-state neutral geometry, perfectly eclipsed with a uniform 4 A interplanar spacing
method: real-time CASSCF Ehrenfest electron dynamics: a fully converged CASSCF calculation is transformed to localized orbitals (hole migration) or natural bond orbitals (exciton migration), and the resulting configuration state functions are propagated in time, with nuclear motion either frozen or coupled through the Ehrenfest gradient
software: development version of Gaussian (Ehrenfest real-time CASSCF implementation)

compound_name: Cyclopropanone, photodissociation to carbon monoxide and ethylene (Norrish-type CO release) plus a polymerization channel
geometry_source: initial conditions from ground-state molecular dynamics sampling at constant excitation energy, mimicking continuous-wave excitation in resonance with the laser; 100 geometries sampled across the spectrum. The cheaper (2,4) active space was used for this ground-state sampling stage
method: a controlled comparison of eight electronic structure methods - SA-CASSCF, SS-CASPT2, MS-CASPT2, XMS-CASPT2, MRCI, FOMO-CASCI, MR-CISD/OM3 and SI-SA-REKS - crossed against several nonadiabatic algorithms (Landau-Zener surface hopping, fewest-switches surface hopping, AIMSWISS), to separate the influence of electronic structure from that of the coupled electron-nuclear algorithm
software: BAGEL for the CASPT2 simulations; other packages per method
basis_set: 6-31G* for most calculations; cc-pVDZ for the CASPT2 runs in BAGEL where 6-31G* is unavailable; a pseudominimal basis by default for MR-CISD/OM3
active_space_orbital_description: two sigma(CC), pi(CO), n(O), pi*(CO) and two sigma*(CC)
active_space_protocol: (8,7) - two sigma(CC), pi(CO), n(O), pi*(CO), two sigma*(CC) - used for every method except SI-SA-REKS. The choice was triangulated three ways rather than assumed: previous studies of this molecule, automated selection with the AutoCAS code, and the authors' own benchmarking of potential energy surfaces and absorption spectra. Two reduced spaces appear for practical reasons: (2,4) for the cheaper ground-state sampling, and (2,2) containing only n(O) and pi*(CO) for SI-SA-REKS, which has no other space implemented. All CASPT2 calculations used a 0.5 a.u. level shift, tested to be insensitive across a wide range. Only S0 and S1 were treated, equally weighted in the SA-CASSCF state-averaging
nroots_per_mult: 2 (S0 and S1, equally weighted)
Other: The paper's central result is that the electronic structure method matters far more than the nonadiabatic algorithm. Excited-state lifetimes across the ab initio family span nearly a factor of two: XMS-CASPT2 39 fs, MS-CASPT2 54 fs, FOMO-CASCI 58 fs, SA-CASSCF 68 fs - a spread the authors call surprising given that the underlying potential energy surfaces differ negligibly. Semiempirical MR-CISD/OM3 is fastest at 36 fs (within XMS-CASPT2 error bars); SI-SA-REKS is an outlier at 90 fs whose population transfer stops abruptly at 140 fs. CO release quantum yields: all ab initio methods agree within error bars and sit close to the experimental 0.73 (intensity-weighted average); MR-CISD/OM3 overestimates at 0.89; SI-SA-REKS fails outright at 0.20 (the authors could not reproduce the 0.44 +/- 0.11 previously published for that method). All ab initio methods find the polymerization channel at least once while the DFT and semiempirical ones never do. By contrast the coupled electron-nuclear algorithms give identical quantum yields within statistical error and consistent population transfer, with FSSH and LZSH essentially equivalent - so when conical intersections are well defined the cheaper LZSH is sufficient.

active_space_protocol: (6,4): pi, pi* and the two nitrogen lone pairs, used identically for XMS-CASPT2, MS-CASPT2 and CASSCF so the methods are compared on equal footing. The reference XMS-CASPT2 used no level shift and had IPEA deactivated. Note the independent convergence on this same (6,4) space for azomethane in 10.1021/acs.jctc.9b00917 and 10.1021/acs.jctc.3c00137, though those papers do not all spell out the orbital composition
Other: Reference XMS-CASPT2 dynamics resolves four time regimes: (I) about 30 fs during which all molecules stay cis on S1; (II) crossing of a first conical intersection region up to about 60 fs, giving 20-25 percent nonadiabatic S1-to-S0 decay and complete cis-to-trans isomerization; (III) a roughly 40 fs plateau with most molecules trans; (IV) a second strong-coupling region with further decay, during which some molecules return to cis. active_space_protocol: A worked example of choosing an active space under a cost ceiling, with the reasoning spelled out. The chemically correct space is (20,16): eight pi plus two nO lone-pair orbitals on uracil, and six pi orbitals on benzene. That space generates 14 158 144 CSFs and 64 128 064 determinants and is affordable only for single points, not for geometry optimization or conical-intersection searches. Dropping the highest unoccupied orbital gives (20,15), 2 186 184 CSFs and 9 018 009 determinants, which the authors identify as the best compromise for vertical excitation energies - explicitly better than the alternative of transplanting the previously used reduced spaces for the separate fragments, (12,9) for uracil plus (6,6) for benzene, which would give (18,15). All geometry optimizations were then done at (20,14), the largest space they could afford for optimization, and MRCI and MS-CASPT2 single points were computed on top of it. 5BU has 106 electrons in 53 doubly occupied orbitals; during MCSCF optimization the lowest 43 orbitals were closed but still fully optimized, and for the correlated single points those same 43 were frozen.

electronic_structure_description: Ground term: S0. Vertical excitation energies in eV, S1 (n-pi*) then S2 (pi-pi*), in the printed order of Table 2: SA-CASSCF(20,14) 4.85 / 7.92; SA-CASSCF(18,14) 4.94 / 5.34; SA-CASSCF(20,15) 5.02 / 7.02; SA-CASSCF(18,15) 4.94 / 5.21; SA-CASSCF(20,16) 4.94 (f = 0.003) / 7.10 (f = 0.571); MS-CASPT2(20,13) 5.02 / 6.83; MS-CASPT2(20,14) 4.93 / 6.28; MRCI(20,14) 5.08 / 7.12; MRCI+D(20,14) 5.11 / 6.90; EOM-CCSD 5.13 / 5.44; LT-DF-LCC2 4.94 / 5.07

Removing two active electrons at fixed orbital count collapses S2 from 7.92 to 5.34 eV at (20,14) versus (18,14), and from 7.02 to 5.21 eV at (20,15) versus (18,15), while S1 moves by only 0.01-0.09 eV. Enlarging the virtual space from (20,15) to (20,16) shifts S2 only from 7.03 to 7.10 eV and leaves S1 unchanged, so the virtual orbitals matter much less than the occupied ones. Dynamic correlation then brings the CASSCF values of 6.93 and 8.48 eV down to 5.83 and 6.93 eV at MS-CASPT2. Because the saturated methylene bridge blocks pi communication between the two rings, the 5BU excited states track the isolated fragments closely: the first two excited states at 5.13 and 5.44 eV match isolated uracil (5.17 eV) and isolated benzene (5.30 eV), and the third and fourth lie at 5.78 and 6.55 eV. compound_name: Ethane (C2H6), C-C single bond dissociation
method: CASSCF followed by MRCI (with the multireference Davidson +Q correction) and the size-extensive averaged coupled-pair functional (ACPF), compared against the single-reference MCPF method

active_space_orbital_description: the full-valence space is (14,14); the (10,10) used here moves one orbital of each of a1g and a2u symmetry in D3d - the symmetric and antisymmetric combinations of the CH bond orbitals that are totally symmetric on each fragment - into the inactive space, with their antibonding partners moved to the secondary space
active_space_protocol: Full valence for ethane is 14 electrons in 14 orbitals, which produced a prohibitively large CASSCF-CI expansion, so a (10,10) was used instead by demoting the totally symmetric CH-bond combinations and their antibonding partners. The authors state they expect MRCI on (14,14) and on (10,10) to give very similar results. The paper's central and directly transferable active-space result: MRCI based on a CASSCF that puts only the electrons of the C-C or N-N bond itself in the active space reproduces full-valence CASSCF/MRCI very well. This worked because the bond orbitals could be cleanly distinguished from those involved in the C-H or N-H bonds. There is in fact more variation among full-valence MRCI results with the reference-selection threshold than between the two choices of active space. The small space carries a second practical advantage: full-valence MRCI and ACPF expansions were prohibitively long and required reference selection (keeping occupations whose spin-coupling coefficients exceeded about 0.05), whereas with the smaller spaces the entire CASSCF could be used as the reference with no selection at all. The authors judge their best numbers to be the ACPF values on the smaller active space, precisely because it avoids reference-selection error.
Other: Single-bonded reference case. The discrepancy between the single-reference MCPF and the multireference ACPF dissociation energies is only 0-1 kcal/mol for single bonds, rising to 3-4 kcal/mol for double bonds and about 6 kcal/mol for triple bonds - consistent with higher excitations mattering more as bond multiplicity increases. All electrons except the 1s on carbon were correlated in the MCPF, MRCI and ACPF steps. The numerical De values are in the paper's Table I, which did not survive PDF text extraction.

compound_name: PTCDA (perylene-3,4,9,10-tetracarboxylic dianhydride), neutral and anion, in flat gas-phase and bent adsorption geometries
geometry_source: two geometries compared: the flat gas-phase structure and the bent geometry the molecule adopts on Ag(110). Adsorption heights of PTCDA on the silver surfaces are known from X-ray standing wave measurements
method: CASSCF with orbital energies approximated as the diagonal elements of the effective Fock matrix in the natural-orbital basis, which under the extended Koopmans theorem can be read as ionization potentials; compared against GGA-level DFT Kohn-Sham orbitals and against orbital energies and momentum patterns extracted from angle-resolved photoemission orbital tomography
active_space_orbital_description: 12 occupied and 12 unoccupied orbitals, defined as natural orbitals of the first-order density matrix; enlarged to 16 occupied and 16 unoccupied in the convergence test, and to 13/12 and 17/16 for the anion
active_space_protocol: Active spaces are specified as a count of occupied plus unoccupied orbitals rather than in (nel,norb) form: 12/12 and 16/16 for the neutral molecule, 13/12 and 17/16 for the anion. The orbital ordering was checked to be robust against how the orbitals are ranked - by occupation number, by using pseudocanonical orbitals, or from state energy differences between neutral and cation - which is what justifies the diagonal-Fock-matrix approximation to the orbital energies. The important negative result is that the ordering is NOT converged with respect to active space size: going from 12/12 to 16/16 makes orbitals D and F swap and E and C swap, and the anion comparison between 13/12 and 17/16 likewise shows convergence has not been reached. The authors present this frankly as the limit of the approach, while noting it also indicates that static correlation among these four orbitals is significant
electronic_structure_description: Experimental reference points: the HOMO emission sits 1.9 eV below the Fermi level and the former LUMO around 0.90 eV binding energy; the orbitals C, D, E and F analysed here lie between 2.8 and 3.7 eV binding energy. The per-orbital computed energies appear only in the paper's figure, not as a text table
Other: The experimental orbital ordering of C, D, E and F, measured consistently across PTCDA monolayers on Ag(110), Ag(100) and Ag(111), disagrees with the DFT prediction. Because the ordering is identical on all three surfaces, it reflects an intrinsic molecular property rather than a substrate effect. Neither the geometric distortion on adsorption nor the extra charge reverses the DFT ordering. CASSCF does change it: with the 12/12 space, orbital F moves to the low binding energy side and orbital C to higher binding energies, agreeing much better with experiment. Treating the anion - justified by the observed 0.5-1.0 electron charge transfer on adsorption - narrows the energy spread of the four orbitals and improves agreement further; for the bent anion the ordering comes close to experiment, with F moved from the high to the low binding energy side.
reference_short: Puschnig et al., Energy Ordering of Molecular Orbitals, J. Phys. Chem. Lett. (2016)
notes: Mined from OA text by claude-casscf-data_mining. software: ORCA (trust-region augmented Hessian TRAH-CASSCF and super-CI-PT SXPT implementations; RIJK or COSX with the DefGrid3 grid for the Fock matrices)
active_space_orbital_description: minimal space containing all Fe(III) 3d electrons and orbitals, five 3d orbitals on each of the two iron centres
active_space_protocol: minimal CAS(10,10) covering all Fe(III) 3d electrons and orbitals; initial orbitals from the model one-electron Hamiltonian followed by AVAS. Active spaces for the transition-metal complexes come exclusively from the AVAS (atomic valence active space) procedure of Sayfutyarova et al., targeting the five 3d atomic orbitals on each metal centre taken from the MINAO minimal basis; double-d-shell guesses are available the same way. The practical appeal is that for a minimal or double-d-shell TMC calculation the only strictly necessary user input is the list of metal centre indices. AVAS supplies both the space definition and starting orbitals coherent with it. For aromatic pi systems the paper uses either broken-symmetry UHF natural orbitals (UNO) or PiAS, a simplified version of the pi-orbital guess of Sayfutyarova and Hammes-Schiffer that builds an inertia tensor over the pi centres and projects the 2p components along the principal axis, so it works for arbitrarily oriented molecules. Point-group symmetry was never exploited anywhere in the paper; active orbitals were localized with Foster-Boys where localization was used.
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: 1Ag
Other: The clearest result in the paper about active-orbital choice: the convergence rate of the second-order TRAH algorithm depends crucially on it. Canonical and natural active orbitals converge slowly, taking nearly 90 iterations; localized active orbitals cut that dramatically. The explanation is chemical - localization disentangles the CAS-CI Hamiltonian into weakly coupled Fe(III) monomer blocks, each qualitatively a single high-spin CSF, which are then antiferromagnetically coupled. That coupled two-monomer CSF carries 98 percent of the weight in the final CI expansion. The first-order SXPT algorithm converged steadily in 19 iterations regardless, showing the AVAS starting orbitals are well matched to the chosen space.
reference_short: A trust-region augmented Hessian implementation for state-specific and state-averaged CASSCF wave functions, J. Chem. Phys. 156, 204104 (2022)
notes: Mined from OA text by claude-casscf-data_mining. d_electron_count is arithmetic from the stated Fe(III) oxidation state. Recorded for the localized-versus-canonical active orbital convergence result on an antiferromagnetically coupled dimer, which is a concrete, transferable piece of guidance for spin-coupled systems.

CAS(12,15): adds the four Gouterman pi frontier orbitals, shown to be crucial for stabilizing the triplet over the quintet. CAS(14,18): NOT an extension of (12,15) - instead it adds four Fe 4s4p orbitals and the remaining three sigma(Fe-N) bonds on top of (8,11), deliberately omitting the Gouterman pi orbitals. CAS(32,34): the largest, containing the entire pi system together with the CAS(14,18) orbitals. CAS(32,34) is too large for conventional CASSCF, so Stochastic-CASSCF optimized its orbitals. Active-space design for transition-metal spin gaps, stated explicitly: small CASSCF-optimized spaces are CAS(6,5) - the five Fe 3d orbitals with six electrons - and CAS(6,10), which adds the five correlating d' (double-shell) orbitals to capture 3d double-shell correlation. compound_name: Ionic-character benchmark set: ethene, butadiene, hexatriene, octatetraene, naphthalene, pyridine, pyrimidine, triazine, acrolein, cyanoformaldehyde, cyclopentadienone (11 molecules, 34 singlet states)
geometry_source: ground-state geometries optimized at CC3/aug-cc-pVTZ
method: state-averaged CASSCF benchmarked against MR-CIS, MR-CISD and MR-CISD with Pople size-extensivity correction (MR-CISD+P), against CC3/theoretical-best-estimate references; the paper introduces the Qat diagnostic of ionic character computed from the transition density
active_space_orbital_description: minimal valence pi/pi* spaces per molecule (see protocol); the paper's whole point is that these minimal spaces fail for ionic states
active_space_protocol: Per-molecule minimal valence pi/pi* active spaces used with SA-CASSCF (states averaged listed in the paper's Table 1): ethene (2,2); butadiene (4,4); hexatriene (6,6); octatetraene (8,8); naphthalene (10,10) for SA-CASSCF/MR-CIS and (8,8) for MR-CISD; pyridine (8,7); pyrimidine (10,8); triazine (12,9); acrolein (6,5); cyanoformaldehyde (10,8); cyclopentadienone (8,7). The central lesson for active-space selection: a minimal pi/pi* CASSCF space overestimates the excitation energies of IONIC states (typically the La / Pariser '+' / bright HOMO-LUMO states) by about 1-2 eV, because ionic states require enhanced sigma-correlation that a pi-only space cannot provide, while COVALENT states (Lb / '-') are described well. Known remedies - doubling the pi active space, adding sigma orbitals, or changing the one-electron basis - all help but it is not obvious a priori when they are needed, and the error often resurfaces even after MRCI or CASPT2. The Qat diagnostic, computed from the transition density, quantifies ionic character and predicts which states will be problematic.
nroots_per_mult: varies per molecule; 34 singlet states total across the set
electronic_structure_description: Aggregate accuracy against theoretical best estimates (aug-cc-pVDZ): SA-CASSCF mean absolute error 0.87 eV for the 34 singlet states; MR-CIS reduces it, MR-CISD gives MAE/MSE 0.27/0.25 eV for singlets, and MR-CISD+P (Pople size-extensivity correction) gives an excellent MAE of 0.11 eV (MR-CISD+P singlet MAE/MSE 0.19/-0.07 eV). Triplet MAEs are largely unaffected by method because triplet states here are covalent. The SA-CASSCF errors correlate strongly with the Qat ionic-character diagnostic.
Other: The paper is a diagnostic/methodology study rather than a chemistry study, but it is unusually directly useful for active-space selection: it demonstrates quantitatively that the failure of minimal pi/pi* CASSCF is specific to ionic states, gives a per-molecule catalogue of which minimal spaces were used, and provides a transition-density metric (Qat) to flag in advance when a larger space or added sigma correlation is required. Ethene is the archetype - its ionic 1Bu singlet is badly overestimated by CAS(2,2) while its covalent 3Bu triplet is fine.
reference_short: Lischka and Plasser, Quantification of the Ionic Character of Multiconfigurational Wave Functions: The Qat Diagnostic, J. Phys. Chem. A 127, 9842 (2023)

geometry_source: H2 at R = 1 a0; CH2 near its conical intersection; LiF across its avoided crossing - all illustrative single points/scans in a 6-31G basis
method: state-specific CASSCF (SS-CASSCF) versus state-averaged CASSCF (SA-CASSCF) and full CI, mapping all stationary points of the CASSCF energy landscape and characterizing their topology (Hessian index, spin contamination)
active_space_orbital_description: minimal (2,2) for H2; also (3,2) tested
active_space_protocol: The paper's transferable message about active-space sizing, stated as a dichotomy: unphysical stationary points on the CASSCF energy surface arise from REDUNDANT orbitals when the active space is too LARGE, and from SYMMETRY BREAKING when the active space is too SMALL. For H2/6-31G, a CAS(2,2) landscape has 25 stationary points (19 singlet, 6 triplet); every exact FCI state has a corresponding SS-CASSCF(2,2) solution, whereas SA-CASSCF(2,2) can only describe the lowest triplet and three lowest singlets, and enlarging to SA-CASSCF(3,2) reaches only the lowest nine excitations. So state-specific CASSCF can capture higher excited states with a MORE COMPACT active space than a state-averaged formalism needs, by using only the orbitals relevant to a given excitation - at the cost of a complicated landscape with root flipping and multiple spurious solutions.

geometry_source: interaction energy curves versus interatomic distance; van der Waals minimum near 5.6 bohr
method: supermolecular CASSCF interaction energies analyzed for their dispersion content, with a derived closed-form CAS dispersion energy (Edisp_CAS) from CAS transition density matrices; benchmarked against SAPT dispersion at the FCI level and an exact reference potential
basis_set: aug-cc-pV5Z for the interaction curves; aug-cc-pVTZ for the long-range C6 analysis

active_space_protocol: A quantitative warning about active-space size and intermolecular dispersion. CASSCF itself recovers a PORTION of the dispersion energy, and that portion GROWS with active-space size, so naively adding a dispersion correction to a supermolecular CASSCF interaction energy double-counts intermonomer correlation by an amount that increases with the space. For He...He: CAS(4,4)+dispersion deviates from the benchmark by only 6.6% at the vdW minimum, but CAS(4,28)+dispersion OVERestimates by 72% and shifts the minimum from 5.6 to 5.3 bohr. point_group: Cs (1A' ground PES; N2O itself linear, NNO = 180.0 deg)
geometry_source: optimized in this work at CASSCF (no analytical CASPT2 gradients in MOLCAS 4.1, so CASSCF geometries were made as good as possible); stationary points first located with (14,12) then reoptimized at CASSCF(18,14); transition-state geometries additionally refined at the CASPT2 level to give approximate CASPT2 structures
method: CASPT2//CASSCF — CASSCF geometries with point-wise CASPT2 single points; transition state theory used for the kinetics
basis_set: Pople Cartesian Gaussian basis sets, chiefly 6-311G(2d) (100 basis functions for the system); 6-311+G(2d) also used for some stationary points
active_space_orbital_description: (14,12)B = all atomic 2p-derived molecular orbitals; (14,12)A = the same but with one 2p-derived MO replaced by one N-2s-derived MO; (18,14)A/B add 4 electrons in two further 2s(N and O)-derived MOs to (14,12)A or B respectively. CI expansion ~85 000 CSFs for (14,12) and ~500 000 CSFs for (18,14) in 1A' symmetry
active_space_protocol: Active orbitals chosen by a natural-orbital-occupation-number (NOON) criterion — keep as active the MOs with NOONs between 0.02 and 1.98 in the state-averaged first-order density matrix, which is argued to give the lowest energy for a fixed CI expansion size. Applied strictly, this criterion gives a DIFFERENT space per reactive channel — (14,12) for the NO+NO channel and (12,10) for the N2+O2 channel — hence inconsistent at, e.g., reactants; the authors instead adopt a homogeneous space over the whole PES even where NOONs fall outside those limits, accepting spaces that are not strictly homogeneous, and aiming at the lowest-energy ground-PES stationary points (NOONs maximally different from 0.0/2.0). Full valence is not feasible for this system, so trial and error plus comparison with experiment was needed. Sequence: (14,12)B all 2p-derived MOs; (14,12)A swaps one for an N 2s MO — needed because nitrogen is a limiting case for which orbitals to make active; (18,14)A/B add two 2s(N,O) MOs (+4 electrons). (18,14)A partitions as O(2,2)+N2O(16,12), i.e. the full valence space of the N2O fragment is correlated. At CASSCF, space A is clearly favoured for (14,12) and the A/B differences shrink for (18,14); once point-wise CASPT2 is applied all four spaces give similar results. B-type spaces were always used in products and describe some regions better
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: 1A' (lowest singlet PES of the O(1D)+N2O system). Orbital No. 8 (U 5f-delta) shows seemingly small orbital entanglement but is included automatically by the selection protocol because it is singly occupied in the electronic ground state

Selection guided by the AUTOCAS state-averaged orbital entanglement diagram: the 5f-delta orbital No. 8 has low entanglement but is auto-included because it is singly occupied in the ground state, in agreement with scalar-relativistic DFT on the same model; the case for the 6p-based orbitals Nos. 1-3 is less clear-cut. Absolute excitation energies are not tabulated in this software-overview article, so no eV values are recorded here

compound_name: Nb3N2 cluster and its cation Nb3N2+ (niobium trimer dinitride)
ligand_set: 2 N atoms bound to a Nb3 triangle (bridging/triply bridging geometries discussed)
point_group: C2v (all calculations performed in C2v; note the arbitrary sigma_v/sigma_v' assignment means B1/B2 labels were swapped to make MOLPRO and GAUSSIAN output consistent)
geometry_source: full geometry optimizations of each electronic state up to the octet, performed in this work in C2v at both B3LYP/srsc (GAUSSIAN03) and CASSCF (MOLPRO-2006) levels
method: CASSCF (Werner-Meyer-Knowles) with single-point MRCI and MRCI+Q (Davidson correction), compared against B3LYP DFT
software: MOLPRO-2006 for CASSCF/MRCI; GAUSSIAN03 for DFT
basis_set: Nb: Stuttgart (srsc) basis with quasirelativistic ECP replacing the first 28 electrons; N: cc-pVDZ. For basis-set tests on the ground states, Dunning bases cc-pVDZ to aug-cc-pVTZ on N with a (10s9p8d2f1g)/[5s5p4d2f1g] basis on Nb
relativistic_treatment: quasirelativistic effective core potential on Nb (first 28 electrons replaced)
active_space_orbital_description: final active space is the 3a1, 2a2, 2b1 and 3b2 orbitals (10 orbitals) lying above the closed 9a1/2a2/5b1/5b2 set, holding 11 electrons (10 for the cation). Nb 4s/4p and N 1s orbitals (6a1, 1a2, 3b1, 4b2) are always doubly occupied
active_space_protocol: Explicit reduction from a full valence space: the full valence active space of Nb3N2/Nb3N2+ is 40 orbitals in C2v (16a1, 5a2, 13b1, 6b2), which gives an intractable number of CSFs. First reduction — the Nb 4s and 4p and N 1s orbitals (6a1, 1a2, 3b1, 4b2) are frozen closed (doubly occupied). The remaining 26 orbitals were still too large, so preliminary CASSCF calculations with a large active space were run and used as a screen: orbitals doubly occupied in ALL configurations were made closed, and high-energy orbitals not occupied in ANY configuration were removed. The resulting space closes the lowest 9a1, 2a2, 5b1, 5b2 and makes active the next 3a1, 2a2, 2b1, 3b2 — 11 electrons (10 for the cation) in 10 orbitals, totalling 7000 CSFs. No excitations were allowed from the closed orbitals but they were allowed to relax. In the MRCI, all CASSCF configurations with absolute coefficients >= 0.05 were used as references, giving up to 125 million configurations
multiplicities_studied: neutral: doublets and quartets at MRCI (geometries optimized for all states up to the octet, 2S+1 = 8); cation: singlets and triplets at MRCI (up to septet optimized)
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: 2B2 for neutral Nb3N2 (1A1 for Nb3N2+). The MRCI leading configuration of each ground state agrees with DFT but accounts for only up to 70% of the total wave function. Excited states of neutral Nb3N2 (eV above ground state): B3LYP puts three states (2A1, 4B2, 4B1) 0.64-0.94; CASSCF puts the first three (2A1, 4B2, 2A2) at 1.0 <= dE <= 1.2; at MRCI and MRCI+Q the 2A1 and 2A2 states rise sharply and only 4B2 remains below 2 eV, so 4B2 is the true first excited state. The 4B2 leading configuration is obtained from the 2B2 ground configuration by exciting an electron from 11a1 into 12a1 and is only 54% of the MRCI wave function. The Nb3N2+ ground 1A1 state is highly multireference with three major configurations. Adiabatic ionization potential (2B2 -> 1A1, removing the unpaired 7b2 electron): experiment 5.44315 eV (ZEKE origin at 43901.7 cm-1, their Ref. 10); this work B3LYP 5.67; MRCI 4.55 and MRCI+Q 4.80 with the smallest basis, MRCI 4.51 with cc-pVTZ on Nb (MRCI+Q unchanged to 3 s.f.); increasing the N basis quality did not affect the IPs
Other: Central finding: transition energies between the neutral and cationic manifolds are predicted POORLY by MRCI relative to the computationally cheap DFT — the MRCI/MRCI+Q adiabatic IPs sit ~0.6-0.9 eV below the very precisely measured ZEKE value while B3LYP is within ~0.23 eV. Adding unlinked quadruple excitations (Davidson) raises the IP by 0.25 eV but not enough. Literature DFT comparisons for the IP: BP86 (ADF) and LSDA (DEMON) both 5.60 eV; B3P86 (GAUSSIAN94) 6.37 eV, ~1 eV too high, consistent with that functional's known 0.3-1.0 eV overestimation. CASSCF and DFT geometries are in general agreement. At CASSCF, the 8A2, 4B1 and 2B1 states are the only ones with triply bridging geometries. A CASSCF-vs-MRCI discrepancy of 2.75 versus 4.75 eV is noted for one state. Geometric, frequency and energetic data for all species are in the supplementary material

compound_name: Nb3C2 cluster and its cation Nb3C2+ (niobium trimer dicarbide), doubly bridging (DB) and triply bridging (TB) isomers
ligand_set: 2 C atoms bound to a Nb3 triangle, in doubly bridging (DB) and triply bridging (TB) arrangements
point_group: C2v (all calculations in C2v; B1/B2 labels swapped for MOLPRO to match GAUSSIAN, see companion row -a)
geometry_source: full geometry optimizations of each electronic state up to the octet, performed in this work in C2v at both B3LYP/srsc (GAUSSIAN03) and CASSCF (MOLPRO-2006) levels; triply bound structures have angle(Nb'NbNbC) < 75 deg with approximately equal Nb-C and Nb'-C bond lengths
method: CASSCF (Werner-Meyer-Knowles) with single-point MRCI and MRCI+Q (Davidson correction), compared against B3LYP DFT
software: MOLPRO-2006 for CASSCF/MRCI; GAUSSIAN03 for DFT
basis_set: Nb: Stuttgart (srsc) basis with quasirelativistic ECP replacing the first 28 electrons; C: cc-pVDZ
relativistic_treatment: quasirelativistic effective core potential on Nb (first 28 electrons replaced)
active_space_orbital_description: final active space is the 4a1, 1a2, 2b1 and 3b2 orbitals (10 orbitals) above the closed 9a1/2a2/5b1/5b2 set, holding 9 electrons (8 for the cation). Nb 4s/4p and C 1s orbitals (6a1, 1a2, 3b1, 4b2) are always doubly occupied
active_space_protocol: Same reduction strategy as for Nb3N2 (companion row -a): the full valence active space of Nb3C2/Nb3C2+ is the same 40 orbitals in C2v (16a1, 5a2, 13b1, 6b2), too large to use directly. The Nb 4s and 4p and C 1s orbitals (6a1, 1a2, 3b1, 4b2) are frozen closed; preliminary CASSCF calculations with a large active space then identified which further orbitals to close (doubly occupied in all configurations) or discard (unoccupied in all configurations), leaving the lowest 9a1, 2a2, 5b1, 5b2 closed and the next 4a1, 1a2, 2b1, 3b2 active — 9 electrons (8 for the cation) in 10 orbitals, 7000 CSFs. Note the a1/a2 split differs from the Nb3N2 case (4a1,1a2 here versus 3a1,2a2 there) even though both end at 10 active orbitals. No excitations from the closed orbitals, but they were allowed to relax; MRCI references are all CASSCF configurations with absolute coefficients >= 0.05
multiplicities_studied: neutral: doublets and quartets at MRCI (all states up to the octet optimized); cation: singlets and triplets at MRCI (up to septet)
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: 2B2 (B3LYP/srsc global minimum, a triply bridging structure). Unlike Nb3N2, Nb3C2 has low-energy doubly AND triply bound structures. At B3LYP the ground-state assignment is ambiguous — four states lie within 0.55 eV, two of them transition states; the two lowest excited states are 3B1 at 0.40 eV and 1B1 at 0.51 eV, both triply bridging. At CASSCF and MRCI+Q the assignment is unambiguous: the next lowest states are 3B2 at 0.62 eV and 1B2 at 0.63 eV, both doubly bridging, and the lowest triply bridging states are 5A1 at 1.51 eV and 3B1 at 1.59 eV (CASSCF). A triply bridging 2A1 search located a transition state with one short and two long Nb-Nb bonds, separated from the 2B2 state by only 1e-5 hartree, indicating Jahn-Teller components of a distorted D3h structure. Ionization potentials (eV, srsc on Nb / cc-pVDZ on C) vs experiment 5.04 (their Ref. 11): MRCI (TB) 2A1 -> 1A1 4.56, MRCI+Q 4.69; MRCI (DB) 2A1 -> 3A2 4.55, MRCI+Q 5.07; B3LYP (TB) 2B2 -> 1A1 5.13; B3LYP (DB) 2B2 -> 1A1 5.93 and 2B2 -> 3A2 5.75
Other: Main chemical conclusion for this cluster: a higher-energy isomer of Nb3C2 may have an electronic transition in the same spectral vicinity as the lowest-energy isomer, which matters for interpreting the observed spectrum (the Nb3C2 spectrum has much richer vibronic structure than Nb3N2). The DB/TB isomer barrier lies between 0.05 and 0.10 eV. As for Nb3N2, DFT electronic configurations agree universally with the MRCI leading configurations, but those leading configurations contribute no more than 70% of the total wave function. One MRCI+Q IP agreeing with experiment is described by the authors as 'fortuitously close'

point_group: C2v used for the state-averaged CASSCF (irreps A1, A2, B1, B2)
geometry_source: ground-state equilibrium geometry optimized in this work; computed R(IBr) = 2.467 (Def2QZVP), 2.460 (aug-cc-pVQZ-PP), 2.473 (ANO-RCC-VQZP), 2.472 A (Sapporo-DKH3-QZP) vs experimental 2.469 A
method: SA-CASSCF / MS-CASPT2 with IPEA shift 0.25 a.u. / SO-RASSI (spin-orbit restricted-active-space state interaction); spin-free and spin-orbit states both reported
software: MOLCAS-family (CASSCF/MS-CASPT2/SO-RASSI approach; program not named explicitly in the extracted text)
basis_set: compared across four: Def2QZVP, aug-cc-pVQZ-PP (ECP), ANO-RCC-VQZP (all-electron) and Sapporo-DKH3-QZP-2012 (all-electron)
relativistic_treatment: all-electron relativistic bases (ANO-RCC, Sapporo-DKH3) and ECP-based bases (aug-cc-pVQZ-PP) compared
active_space_orbital_description: sigma_p and sigma_p* (I 5pz +/- Br 4pz), 2 pi_p and 2 pi_p* (I 5px/y +/- Br 4px/y), 2 pi_d (I 5dxz/yz - Br 4dxz/yz), 2 delta and 2 delta* (I 5dxy/x2-y2 +/- Br 4dxy/x2-y2), and sigma_d (I 5dz2 + Br 4dz2)
active_space_protocol: Active space chosen by combining three sources of information: recommendations from previous theoretical studies, the occupation numbers of quasi-canonical orbitals from initial MP2 computations, and the occupation numbers of natural orbitals from several trial CASSCF computations with different active spaces. This yielded CAS(10,13) for IBr, much larger than in previous theoretical work. Earlier studies used an active space of the Br 4p and I 5p shells only — (10 electrons, 6 orbitals) — or that plus the Br 4d shell — (10,11); the authors note those give good agreement with experiment but argue the iodine 5d orbitals deserve inclusion, giving more symmetric active spaces. Caveat stated by the authors: for a balanced description at the dissociation limit the CAS should include non-truncated p and d shells; since the aim here is transitions at and near the ground-state equilibrium geometry, the CAS was optimised for that region instead
nroots_per_mult: 6 averaged roots in each irrep of C2v (A1, A2, B1, B2)
Other: The 2.44 eV experimental band is only recovered once spin-orbit coupling is included — it corresponds to the (2)0+ (1 3Pi_0+) SO state — which is the central methodological point: SOC is essential for these heavy interhalogens. Deviations of the computed maxima from experiment are not higher than 0.16 eV. Basis-set sensitivity is modest: for the ECP-containing basis sets the VEE and f values do not change appreciably. Oscillator strengths of the SO states vary over orders of magnitude between basis sets for the weakly allowed transitions

active_space_protocol: (10,12) used for both the LS and HS CASSCF wave functions of every complex — five Fe 3d + two eg-like sigma-bonding ligand orbitals + a second diffuse Fe 3d shell. The authors note in closing that the size of the active space is the limiting problem for larger SCO systems and that a restricted active space (RAS) reference would be the way to go beyond this complete-active-space approach

HS-LS electronic energy differences (cm-1) by method — PBE0 / B3LYP / CASPT2 / experiment: [Fe(mtz)6]2+ -3333 / -1822 / 1051 / 120; [Fe(iso)6]2+ -3942 / -2336 / 1062 / n.a.; Fe(phen)2(NCS)2 -4089 / -2551 / 1362 / 719; [Fe(pic)3]2+ -3864 / -2157 / 1320 / 744; [Fe(bpy)3]2+ -726 / 830 / 5807 / ~6000; [Fe(terpy)2]2+ -785 / 713 / 7919 / n.a. Both DFT functionals give the WRONG SIGN (negative, i.e. HS below LS) for most complexes, whereas CASPT2 gives the right order for all of them
Other: Thermodynamics and transition temperatures. Computed Delta_S_HL(T1/2) (J K-1 mol-1), Delta_H_HL (cm-1), experimental Delta_H_HL, computed T1/2 (K) and experimental T1/2: [Fe(mtz)6]2+ 29 / 69 / 120 / 28 / 78 (and 63); [Fe(iso)6]2+ 35 / 149 / - / 41 / 91 (site A); Fe(phen)2(NCS)2 55 / 568 / 719 / 136 / 176; [Fe(pic)3]2+ 51 / 349 / 744 / 82 / 114-121; [Fe(bpy)3]2+ 84 / 5138 / ~6000 / 727 / >450; [Fe(terpy)2]2+ 93 / 7097 / - / 911 / -. The recommended recipe is: compute the HS-LS energy difference with CASPT2 and add DFT vibrational corrections. Zero-point energy corrections (cm-1): -913 for [Fe(iso)6]2+, -794 for Fe(phen)2(NCS)2, -971 for [Fe(pic)3]2+, -669 for [Fe(bpy)3]2+, -822 for [Fe(terpy)2]2+; these vary only ~100 cm-1 with functional or basis set, and the largest contribution comes from the lowest vibrational modes since high-frequency ligand modes are similar in HS and LS. A low-frequency entropy approximation Delta_S_vib = pR ln(nu_LS/nu_HS) using modes below 600 cm-1 gives astonishing agreement for Fe(phen)2(NCS)2 (49 lowest modes: 36.7 J K-1 mol-1 vibrational, 50.1 total vs 49 experimental) and [Fe(pic)3]2+ (36 modes: 59.0 vs 59.5 experimental), but the authors judge this accidental because it fails badly for the other systems and the nu_LS/nu_HS ratio depends strongly on how many modes are included. B3LYP geometries were chosen over the slightly better PBE0 ones because the interpolated CASPT2 optimal Fe-N distance is practically identical for both, frequencies are nearly identical, and B3LYP energetics are slightly better; results are quantitatively very similar with PBE0 throughout. The approach is described by the authors as not quantitative enough for accurate T1/2 but able to reasonably estimate the transition temperature

The paper reports potential energy curves, A 2Sigma+ <- X 2Pi and 2Delta <- X 2Pi electronic transition dipole moments and photodissociation cross sections rather than tabulated excitation energies, so no state energies in eV are recorded here. compound_name: linear SiC3H- anion (and the neutral l-SiC3H radical) — silicon-carbon chain of astrochemical interest
point_group: C-infinity-v (linear; states labelled 1Sigma+, 1Pi, 1Delta, 1Sigma-, 3Sigma+, 3Pi, 3Delta, 3Sigma- for the anion and 2Pi, 2Sigma+, 2Delta, 2Sigma-, 4Sigma+, 4Delta, 4Sigma-, 4Pi for the neutral)
geometry_source: optimized in this work; CASSCF was also used to search for isomers because static correlation can matter for low-stability carbon-chain isomers
method: CASSCF and CASSCF/MRCI (internally contracted multireference CI) for vertical excitation energies and dipole moments; RCCSD(T) and RCCSD(T)-F12 for ground-state properties, with an RCCSD(T)-F12 anharmonic force field via second-order perturbation theory (FIT-ESPEC code)
basis_set: aug-cc-pVTZ for the CASSCF and MRCI vertical excitation energies and electric properties; aug-cc-pV5Z also used
active_space_orbital_description: all the pi-valence electrons were correlated; the core orbitals and the sigma-valence orbitals were considered doubly occupied in all configurations and were optimized. For the electric-property CASSCF calculations on the SiCnH series with 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 carbon atoms, respectively 8, 10, 12, 14 and 19 orbitals were kept doubly occupied in all configurations and optimized during the CASSCF procedure. The paper does not state the active space as an explicit (nel,norb) pair
active_space_protocol: single pi-valence active space, no build-up sequence: all pi-valence electrons active, with core and sigma-valence orbitals doubly occupied but variationally optimized. The number of doubly-occupied (inactive) orbitals is specified per chain length rather than the active space itself — 8, 10, 12, 14 and 19 for SiCnH with n = 1-5 carbons. CASSCF was preferred over RCCSD(T) for the one-electron properties because coupled-cluster wave functions do not satisfy the Hellmann-Feynman theorem in the usual sense, and because for carbon chains with high densities of electronic states near the ground state, expectation values from multiconfigurational methods are 'safer' than monoreferential ones (first observed for C4H)
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: X 1Sigma+ for l-SiC3H- (X 2Pi for the neutral l-SiC3H). Vertical excitation energies (eV) with aug-cc-pVTZ, CASSCF then MRCI. Anion l-SiC3H-: 1Sigma+ 0.0 / 0.0 (E = -493.205588 a.u. at CASSCF, -403.597248 a.u. at MRCI as printed); 1Pi 3.03 / 3.09; 1Delta 4.11 / 3.29; 1Sigma- 3.47 / 3.22; 3Sigma+ 2.57 / 2.48; 3Pi 2.65 / 3.10; 3Delta 2.98 / 2.66; 3Sigma- 3.43 / 2.85. Neutral l-SiC3H: X 2Pi 0.0 / 0.0 (E = -403.139215 / -403.509450 a.u.); 2Sigma+ 2.45 / 2.01; 2Delta 5.99 / 5.66; 2Sigma- 5.42 / 5.43; 4Sigma+ 3.82 / 3.43; 4Delta 4.78 / 3.82; 4Sigma- 5.34 / 4.19; 4Pi 2.77 / 2.21. Dominant configurations are given for every state, e.g. the anion ground state is (11sigma)2(2pi)4(3pi)4 and the neutral ground state (11sigma)2(2pi)4(3pi)3
Other: Astrochemical detection motivation: electron affinities and dipole moments of linear CnSi and SiCnH chains are computed to assess detection probability and anion formation viability. Anions with singlet electronic ground states (SiCH-, SiC3H-, SiC5H-) display significant electron affinities, but their dipole moments — which grow with molecular size — are lower for singlets than for triplets; SiCnH- anions show unexpectedly large dipoles when the electronic ground state is a triplet. Species covered in the comparison are the neutrals SiC (X 3Pi), SiC2 (X 1A1), SiC3 (X 3Sigma-), SiC4 (X 1Sigma+), SiC5 (X 3Sigma-), SiCH (X 2Pi), SiC2H, SiC3H, SiC4H and their anions; almost all are linear except SiC2. An electron affinity of 2.70 eV is obtained with RCCSD(T)-F12A. For l-SiC3H- and l-SiC3D- the absence of previous studies prevents rigorous accuracy conclusions

compound_name: Br2 (bromine molecule) — nonadiabatic transitions among the lower Omega = 1u states and photodissociation
geometry_source: potential energy surface scan performed in this work at CASSCF/aug-cc-pVTZ, giving adiabatic potential curves
method: CASSCF with the time-independent Schrodinger equation for nonadiabatic transitions; time-dependent quantum dynamical method (program of Balint-Kurti et al. 1993) for the photodissociation cross sections
basis_set: aug-cc-pVTZ for the CASSCF potential energy scan; a standard 6-31+G(d,p) basis also used in the CASSCF procedure
active_space_orbital_description: 10 electrons distributed over 8 molecular orbitals: {Br-Br*, x(Br), x*(Br), y(Br), y*(Br), 2 n(Br), Br-Br} — i.e. the Br-Br sigma bonding/antibonding pair, the x and y bonding/antibonding pairs and two bromine lone-pair orbitals
active_space_protocol: (10,8) used throughout, with the orbital composition itemized explicitly; no build-up sequence is described
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: X 1Sigma_g+. Spectroscopic constants, this work vs experiment (Huber and Herzberg 1979; Coxon 1973) — Re (A), De (kJ/mol), omega_e (cm-1), omega_e x_e (cm-1): X 1Sigma_g+ 2.304 / 188.53 / 320.7 / 1.24, experiment 2.280 / 190.17 / 325.3 / 1.08; A 3Pi_1u 2.758 / 22.57 / 144.8 / 2.85, experiment 2.690 / 24.77 / 153 / 2.7; B 3Pi_0+u 2.760 / 43.51 / 163.1 / 1.91, experiment 2.677 / 44.96 / 167.6 / 1.64. Agreement is described by the authors as reasonable
Other: Main result: from configuration analysis of the CASSCF wave functions, the nonadiabatic transition between the two 1u states is a NONCROSSING type, while that between a 1u state and B 3Pi_0+u is a CROSSING type. State correlations: A 3Pi_1u (1u) and 1Pi_u (1u) correlate to the ground-state Br+Br limit, whereas B 3Pi_0+u (0u+) correlates to the Br+Br* limit; a further repulsive 1u state correlating to Br+Br* is implicated in the proposed explanation for the non-limiting beta values observed for the Br+Br* product recoil velocity distributions (Cooper et al. 1998). Absorption cross sections for the ground and lower excited states in the photodissociation of Br2 are presented, along with numerical estimates of nonadiabatic transition probabilities, and the five highest occupied and five lowest unoccupied orbitals of Br2. TD-DFT excitation energies, main excitations and oscillator strengths are tabulated separately for comparison

compound_name: HXeC2H (H-Xe-C(triple)C-H, xenon-inserted acetylene) and the parent acetylene HC2H — excited states underlying the linear and nonlinear optical (L&NLO) properties
geometry_source: excited states computed at the MP2/aug-cc-pVTZ optimized ground-state geometries; equilibrium structure of H-Xe-C(triple)C-H reported at MP2 and CCSD(T) levels (e.g. MP2/aug-cc-pVDZ R(CC) 1.249, R(CH) 1.078, R(XeC) 2.350, R(HXe) 1.750 A)
method: CASSCF/CASPT2 for the excited states (standard zeroth-order Hamiltonian, imaginary level shift 0.2 a.u. to avoid intruder states); transition dipole moments at CASSCF, excitation energies at CASPT2. Complete active space valence bond (CASVB) used for the bonding analysis; MP2 and CCSD(T) for the L&NLO properties themselves
software: MOLCAS 6.0 for CASSCF/CASPT2; VB2000 for CASVB; GAUSSIAN 98 and DALTON also used
basis_set: relativistic ANO-RCC type basis sets contracted to Xe [7s6p4d2f1g] / C [4s3p2d1f] / H [3s2p1d] for the CASSCF/CASPT2; aug-cc-pVnZ (n = 2-5) series for the property calculations, with a small-core relativistic pseudopotential on Xe in some MP2 work
relativistic_treatment: relativistic ANO-RCC basis sets for the CASSCF/CASPT2; small-core relativistic pseudopotential on Xe in the MP2 property calculations
active_space_orbital_description: 3 sigma, 2 pi, 3 sigma* and 2 pi* valence orbitals plus four Rydberg orbitals (one s and three p)
active_space_protocol: Different active spaces were tested to assure the reliability of the results; the final calculations use CASSCF(10,14) comprising 3 sigma, 2 pi, 3 sigma*, 2 pi* valence orbitals plus four Rydberg orbitals (one s, three p). The Rydberg orbitals matter here because the lowest excited state of HXeC2H involves a sigma(Xe-H)* antibonding orbital with diffuse Rydberg-like s character. Separately, CASSCF calculations on the ground states of all studied molecules confirmed that a single electronic configuration dominates the wave function by at least 87%, justifying the single-reference MP2/CCSD(T) treatment of the L&NLO properties
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: closed-shell singlet, dominated by a single configuration (>= 87% in all studied molecules). Key CASPT2 excitation energies for HXeC2H at the ground-state geometry: lowest singlet excited state of pi-sigma* type at 5.32 eV, involving the sigma(Xe-H)* antibonding orbital with diffuse Rydberg-like s character; second singlet excited state of sigma-sigma* character at 6.45 eV. By contrast, in acetylene the low-lying pi-sigma* state (sigma mainly the antibonding CC orbital) is expected above 9.0 eV. Acetylene excitation energies compare favourably with other experimental and theoretical values
Other: Interpretation via a sum-over-states (SOS) perturbative approach connecting excited-state structure to the L&NLO properties. Two striking effects of Xe insertion: (1) it produces much longer/weaker sigma bonds and therefore much lower-energy sigma,sigma*-involving excited states (9.0+ eV in HC2H down to 5.32 eV in HXeC2H); (2) the low-lying valence pi-pi* states are NOT strongly perturbed by Xe insertion and therefore cannot be responsible for the change in NLO property values. The derivatives of interest were synthesized in a Xe matrix, so the local-field (LF) effect of the Xe environment on the properties of HXeC2H was also computed and found significant for some properties. Bonding analysed with CASVB, whose nonorthogonal VB orbitals allow maximum localization without loss of accuracy relative to CASSCF. Effect of Xe core electrons tested by correlating 18 versus 26 electrons explicitly, giving practically the same properties. Experimental harmonic frequencies for H-Xe-C(triple)C-H: 3273, 1748, 1486, 626 cm-1

compound_name: N2O (nitrous oxide) — single-site N1s and O1s double core hole (DCH) states and their Auger decay through CVV to VVVV states; NO also measured
point_group: C2v used in the calculations, although the molecular geometry is C-infinity-v
geometry_source: energies and wave functions of the DCH, CVV and VVVV states evaluated at the experimental equilibrium geometry of the neutral N2O molecule (their Ref. 21)
method: CASSCF and CASCI (complete active space configuration interaction), with Delta-SCF for ionization energies; relative Auger intensities from Wentzel's formula using the full-valence CASCI wave functions of the DCH, CVV and VVVV states
active_space_orbital_description: a total of 12 valence orbitals for N2O; the important sigma, sigma*, pi and pi* orbitals are all included. The 1s core orbitals were kept frozen during all CASSCF orbital optimizations, using the orbitals from a Hartree-Fock calculation on the neutral molecule. The number of active ELECTRONS is not stated
active_space_protocol: full-valence active space of 12 orbitals used for all state classes (DCH, CVV, VVVV), with frozen neutral-molecule Hartree-Fock 1s cores. The substantive protocol choice is the state averaging, which differs per state class: MOs for the CVV states came from state-averaged CASSCF over the lowest 15, 15 and 16 electronic states for the Nt1s-1, Nc1s-1 and O1s-1 CVV states respectively; for the VVVV states, state-averaged CASSCF over the lowest 18 singlet and 22 triplet states. CASCI on top then generated 5000 doublet states for each CVV manifold and 8000 singlet plus 8000 triplet VVVV states. Auger intensities were computed for all possible DCH-CVV transitions (5000 per DCH decay) and, for the CVV-VVVV step, for all pairs involving CVV states with finite DCH-CVV intensity — e.g. 4 500 000 transitions for the Nt1s-2 DCH decay
multiplicities_studied: 1,2,3 (singlet and triplet VVVV states; doublet CVV states)
nroots_per_mult: state-averaged CASSCF over 15/15/16 states for the Nt1s-1, Nc1s-1 and O1s-1 CVV manifolds, and over 18 singlet and 22 triplet states for VVVV; CASCI then produced 5000 doublet CVV states and 8000 singlet + 8000 triplet VVVV states
electronic_structure_description: The states characterized are core-hole states rather than valence excited states: single-site double core hole (DCH) states, core-valence-valence (CVV) states and valence-valence-valence-valence (VVVV) states. Double core hole energies obtained for NO are 904.8 eV (N1s-2), measured at photon energies of 1100 and 1300 eV; for NO the O1s binding energy (IE) is quoted as 1179.4 eV. Spectra were recorded for N2O at the same photon energy (1100 eV) as for NO. A shift of 9.6 eV towards lower binding energy is noted for one feature
Other: Experimental single-site double-core-hole spectroscopy interpreted with the CASSCF/CASCI calculations; the ratio between double ionization energy (DIE) and single ionization energy (IE) is tabulated for NO and N2O. Theoretical values for NO are taken from their Ref. 11 rather than computed here. Contributions are decomposed into relaxation and correlation energy terms, with weighted averages ('av') over singlet and triplet components. Two-electron integrals involving the Auger electron orbital were approximated using MO populations, following their Ref. 12

method: explicitly correlated multireference configuration interaction with Davidson size-consistency correction (F12-MRCI+Q) for the potentials; dipole surfaces at both MRCI and CASSCF; F12-CASPT2 also used for benchmarks. Potentials and dipole surfaces transformed to a diabatic basis with a multiple-property-based diabatization algorithm
basis_set: augmented correlation-consistent aug-cc-pVnZ (n = D, T, Q) with the corresponding standardized auxiliary basis sets
active_space_orbital_description: three nested spaces: sCAS = four electrons in the four pi* orbitals; mCAS = 12 electrons in the pi shell; lCAS = 16 electrons in the p shell. The orbital counts for mCAS and lCAS are not given numerically
active_space_protocol: Three explicitly defined choices, used as a convergence ladder: (1) sCAS — four electrons in the four pi* orbitals, the MINIMAL active space that gives a zeroth-order description of all states of interest, i.e. all states arising from the (pi)4(pi*)2 configuration of the O2 monomers; (2) mCAS — 12 electrons in the pi shell, which additionally captures the static correlation of the pi electrons, important for O2 because of the well-known Hartree-Fock instability associated with artificial breaking of inversion symmetry; (3) lCAS — 16 electrons in the p shell. lCAS is prohibitively expensive at low-symmetry geometries, so the full potential energy and dipole moment surfaces could NOT be computed with it; mCAS is the production space for the surfaces, with lCAS used only for benchmarks at high-symmetry geometries. Benchmarking shows the interaction energy converges reasonably smoothly, albeit slowly, with active space and basis set, so accurate energies are obtainable from affordable MRCI; the transition dipole moment behaves quite differently and depends strongly on the level of theory. Prior systematic work (their Ref. 18) comparing MRCI, CASPT2 and ACPF against CCSD(T) for the high-spin quintet suggests treating MRCI and CASPT2 as upper and lower limits to the potential respectively, with CASPT2 the more reliable; MRCI is nevertheless used here because it gives straightforward access to the transition properties needed for the dipole surface and the diabatization
multiplicities_studied: 3 (seven triplet states of the dimer); monomer states X 3Sigma_g-, a 1Delta_g, b 1Sigma_g+
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: triplet O2(X 3Sigma_g-)-O2(X 3Sigma_g-). Seven triplet states of the dimer are treated. The monomer transitions underlying the collision-induced bands are X 3Sigma_g- -> a 1Delta_g at 7883 cm-1 and X 3Sigma_g- -> b 1Sigma_g+ at 13 122 cm-1. Interaction energies for the seven triplet states are tabulated at the H-shaped geometry at R = 6 a0 using F12-MRCI+Q with all three active spaces and with mCAS F12-CASPT2, but the individual values are not reproduced here
Other: For the triplet ground state of the complex the potential energy surface agrees reasonably with previous calculations, while global EXCITED state potentials are reported here for the first time. Central caveat: the transition dipole moment surfaces depend strongly on the level of theory at which they are computed, as confirmed by the high-symmetry benchmarks, so the authors conclude that ab initio calculations of collision-induced absorption spectra cannot become quantitatively predictive until more accurate transition dipoles are available. The paper also derives the angular expansion of the surfaces and the symmetry constraints on the expansion coefficients, gives working equations for obtaining them by numerical integration over angles, and presents an interpolation scheme with exponential extrapolation to short and large separations for the R dependence
reference_short: Potential energy and dipole moment surfaces of the triplet states of the O2-O2 complex, J. Chem. Phys. 147, 084306 (2017)

compound_name: furan (C4H4O) — photoionization from the ground and excited electronic states, at planar and bent geometries
point_group: C2v for the ground-state (planar) geometry; a bent geometry is also treated
geometry_source: ground-state (planar, C2v) geometry and a bent geometry; the same active space was selected for both
method: CASSCF with NEVPT2 (partially contracted, PC(2) level) corrections for residual dynamical correlation, used to build Dyson orbitals; TDDFT and ADC(2) also used for comparison; continuum dipole matrix elements from a B-spline static-exchange DFT scattering treatment
software: MOLPRO for the HF, CASSCF and NEVPT2 calculations (plus in-house modules); Turbomole for TDDFT and ADC(2)
basis_set: aug-cc-pVDZ (polarization and diffuse functions) for O, C and H; Dyson orbitals projected onto a B-spline basis
active_space_orbital_description: six valence electrons distributed among nine orbitals: one a1, four b1, one b2 and three a2 — comprising 3 occupied (1b1-2b1, 1a2) and 6 virtual (1a1, 3b1-4b1, 7b2, 2a2-3a2)
active_space_protocol: (6,9) used throughout, itemized by irrep (one a1, four b1, one b2, three a2; 3 occupied + 6 virtual), and deliberately kept IDENTICAL for the bent geometry so that planar and bent results are directly comparable. No build-up sequence. Both excitation and ionization energies are then corrected for residual dynamical correlation via partially contracted PC(2)-NEVPT2. For the Dyson orbitals, the overlap between CASSCF wave functions separately optimized for the neutral molecule and for the ion is evaluated, with the N-electron wave function expanded in minors
electronic_structure_description: Ground term: closed-shell singlet in C2v. The valence-shell molecular orbital sequence of ground-state furan is (4a1)2(5a1)2(3b2)2(4b2)2(6a1)2(7a1)2(1b1)2... The paper's quantitative outputs are photoionization cross sections and asymmetry parameters computed from Dyson orbitals rather than a table of vertical excitation energies, so no eV state energies are transcribed here. Ionization energies calculated with the NEVPT2 approach are described as in excellent agreement (with experiment/previous work)
Other: Methodological point: Dyson orbitals are computed at three levels — TDDFT, ADC(2) and CASSCF — and then projected onto a B-spline basis, which decouples the Dyson orbital calculation from that of the continuum dipole matrix elements and lets different electronic structure methods be used interchangeably. The B-spline static-exchange DFT scattering procedure gives a quantitative description of dynamical photoionization observables and generally agrees excellently with experiment. Photoionization from excited electronic states, as well as from the ground state, is treated — relevant to time-resolved photoelectron spectroscopy
reference_short: Ponzi, Sapunar, Angeli, Cimiraglia, Doslic, Decleva, J. Chem. Phys. 144, 084307 (2016)

compound_name: NO + O2 scattering system — multistate electronic quenching of NO A 2Sigma+ by O2, nonadiabatic pathways
point_group: C1 used for the potential energy surfaces in general orientations (unless specified otherwise); Jacobi coordinates used throughout
geometry_source: potential energy surfaces computed in this work over Jacobi coordinates; asymptotic state ordering evaluated at R = 15 A with fixed monomer bond lengths (O2 1.0634 A)
method: state-averaged CASSCF (SA(20)-CASSCF) for the potential energy surfaces, chosen because it models nonadiabatic effects and multiconfigurational character accurately; XMS-CASPT2 with IPEA level shift 0.25 for dynamic correlation; a spline/switched (SW-)CASSCF variant also used
basis_set: t-aug-cc-pVTZ for the SA-CASSCF(19,13) surfaces; t-aug-cc-pVDZ for the XMS-CASPT2(11,9) calculations
active_space_orbital_description: NO and O2 2sigma*, 3sigma, pi_x, pi_y, pi*_x, pi*_y orbitals plus the NO 4sigma orbital, giving CAS(19,13). The reduced space contains only the pi and pi* orbitals together with the NO 4sigma orbital, giving (11,9)
active_space_protocol: (19,13) — NO and O2 2sigma*, 3sigma, pi_x, pi_y, pi*_x, pi*_y plus NO 4sigma — used for the CASSCF potential energy surfaces, with a schematic of the orbital energetic ordering at asymptotic separation given in the paper. (11,9) — only the pi and pi* orbitals plus NO 4sigma — used for the XMS-CASPT2 calculations purely because the full space is too expensive at the CASPT2 level. The number of states is coupled to the active-space choice: because the O2 a 1Delta_g and b 1Sigma_g+ states lie BELOW the NO A 2Sigma+ state, the NO X 2Pi degeneracy couples with the O2 X, a and b states, producing eight doublet and two quartet surfaces below NO A 2Sigma+ + O2 X 3Sigma_g-. The active-space/number-of-states combination was therefore fixed for the spin-doublet states first, giving a minimum of 9 spin-doublet states required, and the production runs used a 20-state average. An IPEA level shift of 0.25 was applied to compensate the usual CASPT2 bias
multiplicities_studied: 2 and 4 (eight doublet and two quartet surfaces below the entrance channel)
nroots_per_mult: SA(20)-CASSCF (20-state average); minimum of 9 spin-doublet states required by the state-ordering analysis
electronic_structure_description: Asymptotic state ordering (R = 15 A, fixed bond lengths), energies in eV, SW-CASSCF then XMS-CASPT2, labelled by NO state / O2 state: A 2Sigma+ / b 1Sigma_g+ 5.569 (CASSCF); X 2Pi / A 3Sigma_u 5.267 / 6.670; X 2Pi / A' 3Delta_u 5.128 / 6.522; A 2Sigma+ / a 1Delta_g 5.095 / 5.582; X 2Pi / c 1Sigma_u- 4.978 / 6.313. Computed with SA(20)-CASSCF(19,13)/t-aug-cc-pVTZ and XMS-CASPT2(11,9)/t-aug-cc-pVDZ
Other: The paper examines how dynamic correlation affects the accessibility and relaxation of the quenching event — comparing SW-CASSCF and XMS-CASPT2 shows dynamic correlation raises the X 2Pi-based channels by roughly 1.3-1.4 eV while affecting the A 2Sigma+/a 1Delta_g channel much less (5.095 -> 5.582 eV), i.e. it substantially reorders the quenching channels. O2 c 1Sigma_u- was suggested by Few et al. (their Ref. 9) as a potential quenching product, which is why the state selection was built around the spin-doublet manifold. Triply augmented Dunning basis sets were chosen as optimized for modelling electronic correlation
reference_short: Soulie, Paterson, J. Chem. Phys. 157, 164304 (2022)
